subject: 6-Bullet Saturday — The Body Lever, Escaping Alzheimer’s, Mental Health Resources, Best Family Trips, and More

bullets.section: Tool I’m using for physical care
bullets.title: The Body Lever
bullets.note: Hat tip to [Nsima Inyang](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mLGqrlxofXA) for introducing me to this self-care contraption. It can be used a thousand ways, but I mostly use it on the legs and low back (e.g., QL and obliques). Who knew you could get so much benefit from putting your muscles in a giant nutcracker?

bullets.title: He Escaped Alzheimer’s Fate. Scientists Want to Know How.
bullets.creator: Pam Belluck
bullets.note:
(_The New York Times_). [Click here](https://archive.is/XNjrW#selection-637.0-641.11) if you have any issues reading the full article at the above link. One of my takeaways: I’ll keep taking those 3–4 sauna sessions a week, based on the mention of heat shock proteins (HSPs). From the article:  
​  
​_Mr. Whitney, 76, is a scientific unicorn with potential to provide answers about one of the world’s most devastating diseases. He has a rare genetic mutation that essentially guaranteed he would develop Alzheimer’s disease in his late 40s or early 50s and would likely die within a decade.  
​  
His mother and nine of her 13 siblings developed Alzheimer’s and died in the prime of their lives. So did his oldest brother, and other relatives going back generations. It is the largest family in the United States known to have an Alzheimer’s-causing mutation.  
​  
“Nobody in history had ever dodged that bullet,” Mr. Whitney said.  
​  
But somehow, he has done just that. Something has shielded him from his genetic destiny, allowing him to escape Alzheimer’s for at least 25 years longer than anyone expected._

bullets.title: Some Practical Thoughts on Suicide
bullets.note:
This post has saved some lives, and I should’ve written it sooner. Read the comments.  
​  
​[**My Healing Journey After Childhood Abuse (Includes Extensive Resource List)**](https://tim.blog/2020/09/14/how-to-heal-trauma/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit) — This includes two very different but complementary approaches.  
​  
If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 (the US Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) or chat [988Lifeline.org](http://www.988lifeline.org/). [Crisis Text Line](https://www.crisistextline.org/): text “HOME” to 741741 to connect with a crisis counselor for free, 24/7 support. If you’re outside of the US, please [click here for a list of international suicide hotlines](http://www.suicide.org/international-suicide-hotlines.html).  
​  
​**And last but certainly not least: call your family and closest friends this weekend.** Check in, tell them you love them, and make a pact that none of you will suffer in silence.
